# Plans and pricing

Tessera Support Cloud is sold in three plans. Prices are per agent seat.

## Free

For teams trying the product. Up to 3 agent seats, email channel only, 1,000 tickets per
month and 30 days of ticket history. Support is community-only: there is no response-time
commitment for Free workspaces.

## Pro

For growing support teams. 19 EUR per seat per month on the monthly plan, or 15 EUR per seat
per month when billed annually. Includes email, chat and web forms, unlimited tickets,
automations, and 2 years of ticket history. Pro customers get email support from our team
during business hours.

## Enterprise

For organisations with compliance needs. Priced by contract, with a minimum of 25 seats.
Includes everything in Pro, plus single sign-on (SAML), audit logs, data residency in the EU,
a 99.9% uptime commitment and a named customer success manager. Enterprise support is
available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week for high-priority tickets.

## Changing plan

# Refund policy

## Annual Pro subscriptions

A new annual Pro subscription can be cancelled with a full refund within 30 days of the
purchase date. After 30 days, annual subscriptions are not refundable, but the workspace
stays on Pro until the end of the paid year.

## Monthly Pro subscriptions

Monthly subscriptions are not refunded. Cancelling stops the next renewal; the workspace
keeps Pro until the end of the month already paid.

## Enterprise

Refunds and credits for Enterprise customers follow their contract. Uptime-related service
credits are described in the SLA article.

## How to request a refund

The workspace owner opens a ticket with the category Billing, stating the invoice number.
Refunds go back to the original payment method within 10 business days of approval.

## Changing plan

Upgrades take effect immediately and are prorated. Downgrades take effect at the end of the
current billing period. Seats can be added at any time; removing seats on an annual plan
only reduces the bill at renewal.

## Service credits

When monthly uptime falls below the 99.9% commitment, Enterprise customers receive a
service credit of 10% of the monthly fee for each full 0.1% below the target, up to 50%.
Credits must be requested within 30 days of the end of the affected month.

# Data retention and privacy

## Where data is stored

Workspaces are hosted in the European Union by default (Frankfurt and Dublin). Enterprise
customers can require that all data, including backups, stays in the EU.

## Retention

Ticket history is kept for 30 days on Free and 2 years on Pro. Enterprise customers choose a
retention period between 1 and 10 years. Attachments follow the same retention as their
ticket. Backups are kept for 35 days and then overwritten.

## Deleting data

The workspace owner can delete a single ticket at any time. A request to delete all personal
data about one end customer (a right-to-erasure request under the GDPR) is completed within
30 days, including backups as they expire.

When a workspace is cancelled, its data is kept for 60 days so that it can be reactivated,
and then permanently deleted.

## Sub-processors

# Support response times (SLA)

These are the first-response targets of the Tessera support team. They apply to tickets
that customers open with us, not to the tickets they handle in their own workspace.

| Priority | Pro | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|
| High (service down, data at risk) | 8 business hours | 1 hour, around the clock |
| Medium (a feature does not work) | 1 business day | 4 business hours |
| Low (questions, how-to) | 3 business days | 1 business day |

Business hours are 08:00 to 18:00 Lisbon time, Monday to Friday, excluding Portuguese public
holidays. Free workspaces have no response target and are answered through the community
forum.

## Escalation

If a high-priority ticket has no answer within its target, reply to the ticket with the word
ESCALATE. It is then routed to the duty manager. Enterprise customers can also call their
customer success manager directly.

## Service credits

ACCOUNT SECURITY

Two-factor authentication
Every agent can turn on two-factor authentication with an authenticator app. Workspace owners
on Pro and Enterprise can make it mandatory for all agents in the workspace settings.

Single sign-on
Enterprise workspaces can sign in with SAML single sign-on (for example Microsoft Entra ID or
Okta). When single sign-on is enforced, password login is disabled for every agent except the
workspace owner, who keeps a recovery login.

Password reset
Agents reset their own password from the login page; the link in the email expires after
60 minutes. Tessera staff never ask for a password, by email, chat or phone.

Locked accounts
After 10 failed login attempts in 15 minutes the account is locked for 30 minutes. A
workspace owner can unlock it earlier from the agent list.

Reporting a vulnerability
Security problems are reported to the security team through the form on the trust page, not
through a support ticket.

## Service credits

When monthly uptime falls below the 99.9% commitment, Enterprise customers receive a
service credit of 10% of the monthly fee for each full 0.1% below the target, up to 50%.
Credits must be requested within 30 days of the end of the affected month.

# Ticket lifecycle

Every ticket in Tessera has one of four statuses.

- **open**: created and waiting for an agent.
- **in_progress**: an agent is working on it. A ticket moves here automatically when an agent
first replies.
- **resolved**: the agent believes the problem is solved. The customer is notified and can
reply to reopen the ticket.
- **closed**: final. A closed ticket cannot be reopened; a new reply creates a follow-up
ticket linked to it.

## Automatic transitions

A resolved ticket closes automatically after 7 days without a customer reply. Replying to a
resolved ticket within those 7 days moves it back to open, keeping its history and priority.

## Priorities

Tickets have a priority of low, medium or high. Priority decides the response target (see
the SLA article) and the order of the agent queue; it does not change the workflow. Only
agents can change a ticket's priority, and every change is recorded in the ticket history.

## Merging tickets

# Ticket lifecycle

Every ticket in Tessera has one of four statuses.

- **open**: created and waiting for an agent.
- **in_progress**: an agent is working on it. A ticket moves here automatically when an agent
first replies.
- **resolved**: the agent believes the problem is solved. The customer is notified and can
reply to reopen the ticket.
- **closed**: final. A closed ticket cannot be reopened; a new reply creates a follow-up
ticket linked to it.

## Automatic transitions

A resolved ticket closes automatically after 7 days without a customer reply. Replying to a
resolved ticket within those 7 days moves it back to open, keeping its history and priority.

## Priorities

Tickets have a priority of low, medium or high. Priority decides the response target (see
the SLA article) and the order of the agent queue; it does not change the workflow. Only
agents can change a ticket's priority, and every change is recorded in the ticket history.

## Merging tickets
